chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from the one who narrated it, from Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar, who said:

I wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him): 'Your Mawla, Ali ibn Mahziyar, bequeathed that Hajj be performed on his behalf from an estate, a quarter of which is designated for you, for one Hajj each year, up to twenty Dinars. And that the road to Al-Basra was cut off, causing the expenses to double upon the people, so twenty Dinars are no longer sufficient. And several of your Mawali have bequeathed similarly regarding their Hajj.' So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'Make three Hajjs count as two, God willing.'
ai.seo_question: How did the Imam adjust the financial requirements for Hajj when costs increased?
ai.summary: This correspondence from Imam al-Hadi (AS) to Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar illustrates the principle of *fiqh al-waqi'* (jurisprudence of context), where the Imam adjusts fixed bequests to account for inflation and disrupted trade routes to Basra. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on practical flexibility (*tawassul*) in fulfilling religious obligations, ensuring that the deceased's Hajj is completed despite economic shifts, rather than being limited by rigid literalism.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from the one who narrated it, from Ibrahim Bin Mahziyar who said,

‘I wrote to Abu Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> that, ‘The one in your<sup>asws</sup> Wilayah, Ali Bin Mahziyar, bequeathed that Hajj be performed on his behalf from a village, a quarter of it being for you<sup>asws</sup>, during every year, one Hajj, up to (expenditure of) twenty Dinars, and the road of Al-Basra is cut off, so the expenditure has increased upon the people, therefore it cannot be sufficed by twenty Dinars. And, a number of the ones in your<sup>asws</sup> Wilayah have bequeathed similarly with regards to their Hajj’. So he<sup>asws</sup> wrote: ‘So make (expenditure of) three Hajjs to be for two Hajjs, (and that would suffice) Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Willing’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from those narrated to him from Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar who has said the following:

“I once wrote to abu Muhammad, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘Your follower, Ali ibn Mahziyar has said in his will to perform al-Hajj on his behalf from an asset of which one-fourth is for you, every year one al-Hajj up to twenty dinar. The road through al-Basra is cut off and the expenses have increased; people charge more than twenty dinar and so also many of your followers have said in their wills. He (the Imam) wrote in answer, ‘Three al-Hajj ah must be made as two al-Hajj by the will of Allah.’”
